title: Harry Houdini: More than Magic
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant profile magician Harry Houdini (born Erik Weisz in Budapest, 1874), covering his childhood poverty and rabbi father, his mother bond, the name change to Harry Houdini (partly after French magician Robert-Houdin), his vaudeville partnership with Bess, his European tour and German court case, signature escapes like the milk can and Chinese water torture cell, the Metamorphosis trick and copyright loophole, his aviation, film career, war on spiritualists including Arthur Conan Doyle and Marjorie Crandon, and his death from appendicitis after being punched by Jocelyn Gordon Whitehead in Montreal. A listener mail correction about recidivism rates from the Mental Records episode closes the show.

segments.title: Opening banter on magicians and Houdini
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether magicians are cool, whether Houdini was cool, their research sources, and their childhood magic phases, plus a tangent about a documentary recommendation.

segments.title: Childhood, father, and mother
segments.summary: The hosts describe Houdini's poverty, his father's failed rabbinical career, his devotion to his mother, and his short stature and athleticism. They cover his birth as Erik Weisz in Hungary, the family's move to Wisconsin, and his name change to Harry.

segments.title: Brothers Houdini, Bess, and early career
segments.summary: Houdini teams with Jacob Hyman as the Brothers Houdini, takes his name from French magician Robert-Houdin, and meets Bess, who becomes his magic partner. The hosts discuss the assistant role and gender norms in magic.

segments.title: Sponsor break and documentary recommendation
segments.summary: A short break in which the hosts recommend the documentary Love on the Spectrum before returning to the show.

segments.title: Vaudeville success and Martin Beck
segments.summary: Houdini and Bess struggle on small venues until Martin Beck, a vaudeville figure, sees a handcuff escape in St. Paul and books them in Omaha. Houdini's publicity stunts with police departments help build his reputation.

segments.title: European tour and German police case
segments.summary: After a falling out with Beck, Houdini and Bess tour Europe and Russia for about five years and become international stars. A Cologne police officer accused him of fraud, and he sued for slander and exposed some tricks in court.

segments.title: Milk can, Chinese water torture cell, and inventions
segments.summary: The hosts describe Houdini's milk can escape and the Chinese water torture cell, his hatred of imitators, and how escapes were staged with timing and sleight of hand, including the key-swap handcuff trick with Bess.

segments.title: Film career, patents, and copyright loophole
segments.summary: Houdini tried movies and produced action films, though his acting was weak. He avoided patents because they required revealing methods, so he copyrighted illusions through plays, including the Metamorphosis trick.

segments.title: Aviation career
segments.summary: Inspired by the Wright brothers, Houdini bought a biplane in Europe, took it to Australia, and became the first person to fly an airplane there.

segments.title: Anti-spiritualism crusade and Arthur Conan Doyle
segments.summary: Houdini opposed spiritualist mediums, was friends with Arthur Conan Doyle until a seance, and fought Marjorie Crandon in Boston with Scientific American and a pamphlet exposing her methods.

segments.title: Death from appendicitis
segments.summary: Houdini fractured his ankle and was punched in the stomach by Jocelyn Gordon Whitehead in Montreal, then performed while ill, and died of a ruptured appendix and sepsis on Halloween 1926 in Detroit. The hosts discuss whether punches cause appendix rupture, plus Bess's seances and conspiracy theories.

segments.title: Listener mail correction on recidivism
segments.summary: A listener corrects Josh's claim from the Mental Records episode that sex offenders have the highest recidivism rate, noting the data does not support it. The hosts acknowledge the error.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and remind listeners of resources and contact information.
